item.title: Ninth Circuit Warns California Employers Implementing Arbitration Agreements Mid-Litigation
item.description: On Jan. 28, 2026, the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals in Avery v. TEKsystems, Inc. affirmed a district court order refusing to enforce an arbitration agreement rolled out during class litigation. The court found that the agreement contained misleading, harmful, and inaccurate information, and that it subverted federal rules by turning the federal class action opt-out procedure into an opt-in process. item.title: AI News: Italy Sets the Rules for AI in the Workplace
item.description: Law No. 132 (the Italian Artificial Intelligence Act) took effect on 10 October 2025.1 Under the Italian AI Act, at least one implementing decree that defines an “organic framework” for data, algorithms and artificial intelligence (AI)-training methods is due by October 2026. item.title: When Trade Becomes National Security: What the Administration’s 2025 National Security Strategy Signals for Companies and Cross Border Business
item.description: The Trump Administration’s release of the 2025 National Security Strategy (the “2025 NSS”) reinforces what has already become evident through policy and enforcement trends: trade, supply chains, and economic leverage are no longer supporting elements of national security policy, but rather its central tools. item.title: U.S. Supreme Court Holds IEEPA Does Not Authorize Presidential Tariffs
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court issued a 6–3 decision today holding that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (“IEEPA”) does not authorize the President to impose tariffs. Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump (24-1287). item.title: AI and Attorney-Client Privilege: Southern District of New York Holds Free Public AI Use Not Protected
item.description: As artificial intelligence (AI) adoption accelerates, so too do the number of headlines highlighting many new legal risks these tools present. item.title: FERC Takes Action to Streamline its Environmental Review of Hydropower Projects
item.description: Introduction In its Open Meeting on February 19, 2026, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) took two actions to streamline the environmental review of hydropower projects.
